title: Linear Independence of {1, ∛3, (∛3)²} over ℚ
description: Proves {1, ∛3, (∛3)²} is linearly independent over ℚ via a minimal polynomial degree argument: any ℚ-linear combination aeval α p = 0 forces the degree-≤2 polynomial p to be divisible by minpoly ℚ α (degree 3), hence p = 0 and all coefficients vanish.

overview.historicalContext: Linear independence of {1, ∛3, (∛3)²} over ℚ is a classical consequence of algebraic number theory. It expresses that ∛3 has degree exactly 3 over ℚ — meaning ∛3 satisfies no polynomial equation over ℚ of degree less than 3. This was known in principle from Galois theory (Eisenstein, 1850s), though the explicit linear independence statement became a standard exercise once field extension theory was systematized by Dedekind and Kronecker in the latter half of the 19th century.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question OQ-02 from cube-root-3-irrational-oq-02:**

The parent entry proves ∛3 is irrational via Eisenstein's irreducibility criterion: X³-3 is irreducible over ℚ, so it has no rational roots. The natural follow-up: can we prove the stronger statement that {1, ∛3, (∛3)²} is linearly independent over ℚ?

**This file answers yes.** The key is that linear independence of {α^0, α^1, α^2} is equivalent to: the only ℚ-polynomial of degree ≤ 2 with α as a root is the zero polynomial. This follows immediately from minpoly ℚ α having degree 3.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Core argument** (by contradiction):

Suppose Σᵢ cᵢ · αⁱ = 0 for c₀, c₁, c₂ : ℚ. Define p = C(c₀) + C(c₁)X + C(c₂)X² ∈ ℚ[X]. Then:

1. **aeval α p = 0** (by unfolding the polynomial evaluation).
2. **minpoly ℚ α ∣ p** (by `minpoly.dvd`, since aeval α p = 0).
3. **natDegree(minpoly ℚ α) = 3** (from `minpoly_nthRoot_natDegree 3 3 3`, Eisenstein at p=3).
4. **natDegree(p) ≤ 2** (p has terms at positions 0, 1, 2 only).
5. If p ≠ 0: `natDegree_le_of_dvd` gives 3 = natDegree(minpoly) ≤ natDegree(p) ≤ 2. Contradiction.
6. So p = 0, hence c₀ = coeff(p, 0) = 0, c₁ = coeff(p, 1) = 0, c₂ = coeff(p, 2) = 0.
keyInsights: The minpoly divisibility `minpoly.dvd ℚ α h` converts the evaluation condition aeval α p = 0 into the algebraic divisibility condition minpoly ℚ α | p
The degree bound natDegree(p) ≤ 2 uses natDegree_add_le + natDegree_mul_le + natDegree_C = 0 + natDegree_X_pow = n iteratively
natDegree_le_of_dvd gives the critical inequality: if q | p and p ≠ 0 then natDegree q ≤ natDegree p
The coefficient extraction coeff(p, i) = cᵢ is verified by fin_cases + simp: the polynomial C(c₀) + C(c₁)X + C(c₂)X² has exactly cᵢ at position i for i ∈ {0,1,2}
Fintype.linearIndependent_iff reformulates the goal as: ∀ c : Fin 3 → ℚ, (Σ cᵢ • αⁱ = 0) → (∀ i, cᵢ = 0), cleanly separating construction from extraction
prerequisites: Polynomial natDegree bounds: natDegree_add_le, natDegree_mul_le, natDegree_C, natDegree_X_pow

conclusion.summary: {1, ∛3, (∛3)²} is ℚ-linearly independent via minpoly divisibility. 2 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications:
**Stronger than irrationality**: ∛3 ∉ ℚ says the degree-1 polynomial X - ∛3 has no ℚ coefficients. Linear independence says no nonzero degree-≤2 polynomial over ℚ has ∛3 as a root. This is equivalent to minpoly ℚ (∛3) having degree exactly 3.

**Basis for the degree-3 extension**: Together with (∛3)³ = 3 ∈ ℚ, linear independence shows {1, ∛3, (∛3)²} spans ℚ(∛3) over ℚ. So {1, ∛3, (∛3)²} is a ℚ-basis for ℚ(∛3), giving an alternative proof of [ℚ(∛3):ℚ] = 3.

**Generalizes**: The same minpoly divisibility argument works for any α with natDegree(minpoly ℚ α) = n: the set {1, α, ..., α^(n-1)} is ℚ-linearly independent.
openQuestions: Can the same argument prove {1, ∛m, (∛m)²} is linearly independent for any m with a squarefree prime factor? (Yes: minpoly_nthRoot_natDegree from CubeRoot2IrrationalOQ03 gives the same degree-3 bound.)
Is {1, α, ..., α^(n-1)} linearly independent whenever natDegree(minpoly ℚ α) = n? (Yes, by the same argument — this is essentially the definition of having degree-n minimal polynomial.)
